cards.front: Why can P. vivax and P. ovale malaria return months after successful treatment?
cards.back: Both species leave dormant **hypnozoites** in the **liver**. Blood-stage drugs do not kill them, so they can reactivate later. A liver-stage drug (**primaquine** or tafenoquine) is added, after testing for **G6PD deficiency**, because these drugs can cause hemolysis.
cards.back_pt: As duas espécies deixam **hipnozoítos** latentes no **fígado**. Os fármacos que agem na fase sanguínea não os eliminam, e eles podem reativar depois. Acrescenta-se um fármaco contra a fase hepática (**primaquina** ou tafenoquina), após testar **deficiência de G6PD**, pois esses fármacos podem causar hemólise.

cards.front: Why does Plasmodium falciparum cause the most severe malaria?
cards.back: Infected RBCs display adhesion proteins (**PfEMP1**) and stick to small-vessel **endothelium** in the brain, kidney and placenta (**cytoadherence**). It invades RBCs of any age, so parasitemia can be very high. Smear: many small **ring forms** and **crescent-shaped gametocytes**.
cards.back_pt: As hemácias infectadas expõem proteínas de adesão (**PfEMP1**) e aderem ao **endotélio** de pequenos vasos no cérebro, rim e placenta (**citoaderência**). O parasita invade hemácias de qualquer idade, então a parasitemia pode ser muito alta. Esfregaço: muitas **formas em anel** pequenas e **gametócitos em forma de crescente** (em banana).

cards.front: Which tick-borne protozoan infects red cells, and what does its blood smear show?
cards.back: *Babesia microti*, spread by the **Ixodes tick** (the same tick as Lyme disease), mainly in the northeastern US. It causes fever and **hemolytic anemia**, severe in **asplenic** patients. Smear: rings and **tetrads** (*Maltese cross*), with no malaria pigment.
cards.back_pt: *Babesia microti*, transmitida pelo **carrapato Ixodes** (o mesmo da doença de Lyme), principalmente no nordeste dos EUA. Causa febre e **anemia hemolítica**, grave em pacientes **asplênicos**. Esfregaço: anéis e **tétrades** (*Maltese cross*, cruz de Malta), sem o pigmento da malária.

cards.front: How is Trypanosoma cruzi transmitted, and what are the late effects of Chagas disease?
cards.back: The **triatomine (kissing) bug** defecates while it feeds; parasites in the **feces** enter the bite or the conjunctiva (**Romaña sign**). Also spread by contaminated food, blood and the placenta. Chronic phase: **dilated cardiomyopathy**, **megaesophagus** and **megacolon**.
cards.back_pt: O **triatomíneo (barbeiro)** defeca enquanto se alimenta; os parasitas nas **fezes** penetram pela picada ou pela conjuntiva (**sinal de Romaña**). Também há transmissão por alimentos contaminados, sangue e placenta. Fase crônica: **cardiomiopatia dilatada**, **megaesôfago** e **megacólon**.

cards.front: What causes kala-azar, and what does a bone marrow or spleen aspirate show?
cards.back: *Leishmania donovani* complex (*L. infantum* in Brazil), spread by the **sandfly**. It causes fever, weight loss, **massive splenomegaly** and **pancytopenia**. The aspirate shows **amastigotes** inside **macrophages**.
cards.back_pt: Complexo *Leishmania donovani* (*L. infantum* no Brasil), transmitido pelo **flebotomíneo** (mosquito-palha). Causa febre, emagrecimento, **esplenomegalia volumosa** e **pancitopenia**. O aspirado mostra **amastigotas** dentro de **macrófagos**. É o **calazar**.

cards.front: How do humans become infected with Toxoplasma gondii?
cards.back: **Cats** are the definitive host and shed **oocysts** in their feces. Humans swallow oocysts (cat litter, soil, unwashed vegetables, water) or **tissue cysts** in **undercooked meat**. A first infection during **pregnancy** can cross the placenta.
cards.back_pt: Os **gatos** são o hospedeiro definitivo e eliminam **oocistos** nas fezes. O ser humano ingere oocistos (caixa de areia, solo, verduras mal lavadas, água) ou **cistos teciduais** em **carne malcozida**. Uma primoinfecção na **gestação** pode atravessar a placenta.

cards.front: A healthy child dies a week after swimming in a warm freshwater lake. Which parasite is likely, and how does it reach the brain?
cards.back: *Naegleria fowleri*. The amoeba enters the nose and follows the **olfactory nerve** through the **cribriform plate**. It causes a rapidly fatal **primary amebic meningoencephalitis**. CSF may show motile trophozoites.
cards.back_pt: *Naegleria fowleri*. A ameba entra pelo nariz e segue o **nervo olfatório** através da **lâmina cribriforme**. Causa uma **meningoencefalite amebiana primária** rapidamente fatal. O LCR pode mostrar trofozoítos móveis.

cards.front: Why can Strongyloides stercoralis cause a fatal infection decades after the patient left an endemic area?
cards.back: Its larvae can become infective inside the gut and reinvade through the bowel wall or perianal skin (**autoinfection**), so infection lasts for life. **Corticosteroids** or **HTLV-1** can trigger **hyperinfection**: massive larval spread and gram-negative sepsis. Stool shows **larvae**, not eggs.
cards.back_pt: As larvas podem se tornar infectantes ainda no intestino e reinvadir pela parede intestinal ou pela pele perianal (**autoinfecção**), então a infecção persiste por toda a vida. **Corticoides** ou **HTLV-1** podem desencadear **hiperinfecção**: disseminação maciça de larvas com sepse por gram-negativos da flora intestinal. As fezes mostram **larvas**, não ovos.

questions.stem: A 34-year-old man from a rural area of northeastern Brazil has a feeling of fullness in the left upper abdomen. As a child, he often swam and fished in a slow river. Exam shows a firm, enlarged liver and a large spleen. Upper endoscopy shows esophageal varices. Albumin, bilirubin and liver enzymes are normal. Stool microscopy shows large oval eggs with a prominent lateral spine. Which organism is most likely responsible?
questions.explanation: Cercariae released by freshwater **snails** penetrate the skin. *S. mansoni* adults live in the mesenteric veins, and their eggs (with a **lateral spine**) lodge in portal venules and cause granulomas and **periportal (pipestem) fibrosis**. This gives **presinusoidal portal hypertension** with normal liver function. *S. haematobium* eggs have a **terminal spine** and appear in the urine. Liver flukes (*Fasciola*, *Clonorchis*) live in the bile ducts and have operculated eggs without a spine.
questions.explanation_pt: As cercárias liberadas por **caramujos** de água doce penetram a pele. Os vermes adultos de *S. mansoni* vivem nas veias mesentéricas, e seus ovos (com **espícula lateral**) ficam retidos nas vênulas portais e causam granulomas e **fibrose periportal** (de Symmers, *pipestem*). Isso gera **hipertensão portal pré-sinusoidal** com função hepática normal. Os ovos de *S. haematobium* têm **espícula terminal** e aparecem na urina. *Fasciola* e *Clonorchis* vivem nas vias biliares e têm ovos operculados sem espícula.

questions.stem: A 45-year-old sheep farmer from southern Brazil has had dull right upper quadrant pain for several months. He has no fever. His dogs are often fed the organs of slaughtered sheep. CT shows a large cyst in the right lobe of the liver with a partly calcified wall and several smaller cysts inside it. The eosinophil count is mildly increased. Which organism is the most likely cause?
questions.explanation: **Dogs** carry the adult *Echinococcus* tapeworm after eating infected sheep organs; humans swallow eggs from dog feces. The larvae form a slowly growing **hydatid cyst** with **daughter cysts**, usually in the liver. Spilling the cyst fluid can cause **anaphylaxis**. An amebic liver abscess usually causes fever and has no daughter cysts or wall calcification.
questions.explanation_pt: Os **cães** abrigam o verme adulto de *Echinococcus* após comerem vísceras de ovinos infectados; o ser humano ingere ovos presentes nas fezes dos cães. As larvas formam um **cisto hidático** de crescimento lento, com **vesículas filhas**, geralmente no fígado. O extravasamento do líquido do cisto pode causar **anafilaxia**. O abscesso hepático amebiano costuma causar febre e não tem vesículas filhas nem calcificação da parede.

questions.stem: A 22-year-old man recently moved to the United States from a rural farming area in Central America, where he worked barefoot. He has fatigue and shortness of breath on exertion. Months ago he had an itchy rash on his feet, followed by a dry cough. Hemoglobin is 8.9 g/dL, MCV is 68 fL, and eosinophils are 9%. Stool microscopy shows thin-shelled oval eggs. Which organism is most likely responsible?
questions.explanation: Hookworm larvae in soil **penetrate the skin** (itchy rash), pass through the lungs (cough) and attach to the small bowel wall, where the adults **suck blood**. Chronic blood loss causes **iron deficiency (microcytic) anemia**. *Strongyloides* also enters through the skin, but its stool finding is **larvae**, not eggs, and anemia is not typical.
questions.explanation_pt: As larvas de ancilostomídeos no solo **penetram a pele** (erupção pruriginosa), passam pelos pulmões (tosse) e se fixam na parede do intestino delgado, onde os adultos **sugam sangue**. A perda crônica de sangue causa **anemia ferropriva (microcítica)**; por isso a ancilostomíase é chamada popularmente de "amarelão". *Strongyloides* também penetra pela pele, mas nas fezes aparecem **larvas**, não ovos, e anemia não é típica.

questions.stem: A 38-year-old man has fever, muscle pain and swelling around both eyes. Three weeks ago he went hunting and ate homemade wild boar sausage. Two weeks ago he had a few days of diarrhea. Exam shows periorbital edema, splinter hemorrhages under the nails, and tender calf and arm muscles. Eosinophils are 30%, and creatine kinase is high. Which organism is most likely responsible?
questions.explanation: *Trichinella* larvae are encysted in **undercooked pork or wild game**. After a brief intestinal phase, new larvae travel in the blood and encyst in **striated muscle**, causing **myositis**, **periorbital edema** and marked **eosinophilia**. *Toxoplasma* can also come from undercooked meat, but it does not cause this myositis with marked eosinophilia. Eating pork tapeworm cysts gives only an intestinal *Taenia solium* worm; cysticercosis needs ingested eggs.
questions.explanation_pt: As larvas de *Trichinella* ficam encistadas em **carne de porco ou de caça malcozida**. Após uma breve fase intestinal, novas larvas circulam no sangue e se encistam no **músculo estriado**, causando **miosite**, **edema periorbitário** e **eosinofilia** intensa. *Toxoplasma* também pode vir de carne malcozida, mas não causa essa miosite com eosinofilia intensa. Comer cisticercos na carne de porco gera apenas a *Taenia solium* intestinal; a cisticercose exige a ingestão de ovos.

notes.title: Parasitology: protozoa, worms and their exposures
notes.body_md:
## Intestinal and free-living protozoa

- **Giardia** (fatty diarrhea), **Entamoeba** (flask-shaped ulcers, liver abscess) and **Cryptosporidium** (acid-fast oocysts, AIDS): see the GI infections block.
- **Naegleria**: warm fresh water, nose to brain through the **cribriform plate**; fatal meningoencephalitis.
- **Acanthamoeba**: **contact lens keratitis**; slow encephalitis in the immunocompromised.
- **Trichomonas vaginalis**: motile flagellated trophozoites (see the STI block).

## Blood and tissue protozoa

- **Plasmodium** (*Anopheles* mosquito): *vivax*/*ovale* have **hypnozoites** and 48-hour fever cycles; *malariae* 72-hour cycles; *falciparum* is the most severe. **Duffy-negative** red cells largely resist *vivax*; **sickle trait** protects against *falciparum*.
- **Babesia**: *Ixodes* tick; *Maltese cross*; worse after splenectomy.
- **Toxoplasma**: cat feces or undercooked meat; ring-enhancing brain lesions in AIDS; congenital infection.
- **Trypanosoma brucei**: **tsetse fly** (Africa); **sleeping sickness**; waves of fever from **antigenic variation**.
- **Trypanosoma cruzi**: **triatomine bug**; Chagas disease (heart, esophagus, colon).
- **Leishmania**: **sandfly**; skin ulcers or visceral disease (**kala-azar**).

## Nematodes (roundworms)

- Eggs swallowed: **Enterobius** (night-time perianal itch, *scotch tape test*), **Ascaris** (bowel obstruction), **Toxocara** (dog or cat feces; *visceral larva migrans*).
- Larvae in meat: **Trichinella** (myositis).
- Through the skin: **hookworms** (iron deficiency anemia), **Strongyloides** (autoinfection).
- By insects: **Wuchereria** (mosquito; lymphatic filariasis), **Onchocerca** (blackfly; **river blindness**), **Loa loa** (deer fly; worm seen crossing the eye).

## Cestodes (tapeworms)

- **Taenia solium**: cysts in pork give an intestinal worm; swallowed eggs give **cysticercosis** (seizures). **T. saginata**: beef; intestinal only.
- **Diphyllobothrium latum**: raw freshwater fish; **vitamin B12 deficiency**.
- **Echinococcus**: eggs from dog feces; **hydatid cyst**; rupture can cause **anaphylaxis**.

## Trematodes (flukes)

- Freshwater **snails** are intermediate hosts for *Schistosoma*.
- **S. mansoni**: periportal fibrosis and portal hypertension (common in Brazil).
- **S. haematobium**: hematuria and **bladder squamous cell carcinoma**.
- **Clonorchis**: raw fish; **cholangiocarcinoma**.

## Pointers

- Scabies and lice: skin block. Antiparasitic drugs: antimicrobial pharmacology block.
notes.body_pt_md:
## Protozoários intestinais e de vida livre

- **Giardia** (diarreia gordurosa), **Entamoeba** (úlceras em forma de frasco (em botão de camisa); abscesso hepático) e **Cryptosporidium** (oocistos álcool-ácido resistentes, aids): ver o bloco de infecções GI.
- **Naegleria**: água doce morna, do nariz ao cérebro pela **lâmina cribriforme**; meningoencefalite fatal.
- **Acanthamoeba**: **ceratite em usuários de lentes de contato**; encefalite lenta em imunocomprometidos.
- **Trichomonas vaginalis**: trofozoítos flagelados móveis (ver o bloco de IST).

## Protozoários do sangue e dos tecidos

- **Plasmodium** (mosquito *Anopheles*): *vivax*/*ovale* têm **hipnozoítos** e ciclos febris de 48 horas; *malariae*, ciclos de 72 horas; *falciparum* é o mais grave. Hemácias **Duffy-negativas** resistem em grande parte ao *vivax*; o **traço falciforme** protege contra o *falciparum*.
- **Babesia**: carrapato *Ixodes*; cruz de Malta (*Maltese cross*); pior após esplenectomia.
- **Toxoplasma**: fezes de gato ou carne malcozida; lesões cerebrais com realce anelar na aids; infecção congênita.
- **Trypanosoma brucei**: **mosca tsé-tsé** (África); **doença do sono**; ondas de febre por **variação antigênica**.
- **Trypanosoma cruzi**: **triatomíneo (barbeiro)**; doença de Chagas (coração, esôfago, cólon).
- **Leishmania**: **flebotomíneo** (mosquito-palha); úlceras cutâneas ou doença visceral (**calazar**).

## Nematódeos (vermes cilíndricos)

- Ovos ingeridos: **Enterobius** (prurido anal noturno, método da fita adesiva de Graham, *scotch tape test*), **Ascaris** (obstrução intestinal), **Toxocara** (fezes de cão ou gato; *larva migrans visceral*).
- Larvas na carne: **Trichinella** (miosite).
- Pela pele: **ancilostomídeos** (anemia ferropriva), **Strongyloides** (autoinfecção).
- Por insetos: **Wuchereria** (mosquito; filariose linfática), **Onchocerca** (borrachudo; **cegueira dos rios**), **Loa loa** (mutuca; verme visto atravessando o olho).

## Cestódeos (tênias)

- **Taenia solium**: cisticercos na carne de porco geram o verme intestinal; ovos ingeridos causam **cisticercose** (crises epilépticas). **T. saginata**: carne bovina; apenas intestinal.
- **Diphyllobothrium latum**: peixe de água doce cru; **deficiência de vitamina B12**.
- **Echinococcus**: ovos nas fezes de cães; **cisto hidático**; a ruptura pode causar **anafilaxia**.

## Trematódeos (vermes achatados não segmentados)

- **Caramujos** de água doce são hospedeiros intermediários do *Schistosoma*.
- **S. mansoni**: fibrose periportal e hipertensão portal (comum no Brasil).
- **S. haematobium**: hematúria e **carcinoma de células escamosas da bexiga**.
- **Clonorchis**: peixe cru; **colangiocarcinoma**.

## Referências cruzadas

- Escabiose e pediculose: bloco de pele. Antiparasitários: bloco de farmacologia antimicrobiana.
